correctness.rationale: For acute ABC and any X,Y,Z on closed sides, cosine rule gives ZX=sqrt(u²+p²), XY=sqrt(v²+q²), YZ=sqrt(w²+r²) for the explicitly given linear forms. The telescoping u+v+w=a cos A+b cos B+c cos C=8Delta²/(abc) yields exact nonnegative remainder. For zero deficit, p=q=r=0; solving the sine-rule linear system gives unique orthic x0=c cos B, y0=a cos C, z0=b cos A, and positivity of linear components at orthic. Rationalization sqrt(s²+t²)-s=t²/(sqrt(s²+t²)+s), with degenerate t=0 handled separately, and each chord <=D proves deficit >=(p²+q²+r²)/(2D). With U=sin A(x-x0),V=sin B(y-y0),W=sin C(z-z0), p=U+W,q=U+V,r=V+W, hence p²+q²+r²=(U+V+W)²+U²+V²+W²>=U²+V²+W². Independently tested acute triangles including equilateral and 200 random side placements each; exact identity errors <=2.22e-15, inequality margins nonnegative. Computation is not universal proof.
